      # MiniSketch — architecture guide
      
      Read this before changing code. It exists so the next developer (human or AI)
      knows the data model, the invariants that have already caused real bugs, and
      where each kind of change belongs.
      
      ## How it runs
      
      Plain static files, no build step, opened straight from disk
      (`file://…/index.html`). That is a hard constraint:
      
      - **No ES modules** (`import`/`export` is blocked over `file://` in Chrome).
        Files are classic `<script>` tags loaded in order: `tools/imagetracer.js`,
        `tools/clipper.js`, `tools/registry.js`, the tool files (`tools/box.js`,
        `tools/slot.js`, `tools/gear.js`, `tools/wall.js`), `core.js`, `app.js`.
      - `core.js` is pure (no DOM, no app state) and doubles as a Node module so
        `tests/smoke.js` can run it.
      
      ## Files
      
      | File | What lives there |
      | --- | --- |
      | `core.js` | Pure math: scalars, matrices, SVG path parsing, cubic/spline sampling, the LM solver, polygon/chain utilities, serialization rounding. Global functions. |
      | `app.js` | The whole application in one IIFE: document state, rendering, hit-testing, tools/commands, solver wiring, import/export, CNC, UI. |
      | `index.html` | Layout, menus, modals, the bilingual Help text. |
      | `styles.css` | All styling. |
      | `tools/` | `registry.js` + one file per generator (`box.js`, `slot.js`, `gear.js`, `wall.js`, `hinge.js`, …), the tracer (`trace.js`, our wrapper) and the vendored libraries (`imagetracer.js`, `clipper.js`). Do not edit the vendored ones. |
      | `fonts/` | The Text dialog's font catalogue. `fonts.js` is the registry (lazy loader, IndexedDB for imported fonts, `FONT_EPOCH`); `build.js` turns `fonts/src/*.ttf` into one generated `fonts/<slug>.js` per face (base64 bytes, registered through `FontFace` — the only route that works from `file://`); `hershey-data.js` + `hershey.js` are the public-domain single-line (stroke) fonts. Do not hand-edit the generated files or `hershey-data.js`. |
      | `TOOLS.md` | How to write a tool/plugin: the registration contract, the whole `api` surface, conventions, and testing. |
      | `testing/` | Standalone probes (`node testing/<name>_probe.js`). They slice functions out of the sources and run them without a DOM. `tools_probe.js` checks every registered tool against the contract. |
      | `tests/smoke.js` | `node tests/smoke.js` — regression tests for `core.js`. |
      | `server/` | The AI bridge (`ai-bridge.js`) and a dev static server. The bridge is the ONLY place a paid LLM call happens. |
      
      ## The AI endpoint is BYOK
      
      **There is no API key in this repository.** A key baked into the source leaks
      with the source, so the bridge starts with none and takes one from the user.
      
      The key travels this way:
      
      1. **MiniSketch Settings › AI chat** holds `AI API base URL`, `AI API key`
         (a masked field) and `AI model`. The app sends all three with every
         `/api/chat` request, in a `settings` block.
      2. The bridge uses them **for that request only** and keeps no copy.
      3. `POST /api/settings` on the bridge stores the same three values in memory
         (gone when the bridge stops) — for a bridge that serves several people.
      4. `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `MODEL` in `server/.env` are the
         fallback for a bridge run by one person.
      
      Order of precedence: request → bridge settings → environment. With no key at
      all the bridge answers **400** and names the setting to fill — it must never
      fail silently.
      
      **CORS is an allowlist, not `*`.** `originAllowed()` accepts a local file
      (`Origin: null`, i.e. the app opened from disk), any `localhost` /
      `127.0.0.1` port, and a private LAN address (the phone or tablet talking to
      this PC). Everything else gets **403**. `AI_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` adds exact
      origins. Without this, any web page the user visits could spend their key
      through their own bridge.
      
      `testing/ai_bridge_probe.js` pins all of it (33 checks).
      
      ## Data model (`state`)
      
      ```
      state = {
        points:      { id: { x, y } },              // world mm, Y goes up
        entities:    { id: entity },                // see below
        constraints: { id: constraint },
        namedSel:    { name: [{ kind, id }, …] },
        layers:      [{ id, name, visible, locked }],
        nextLayerId, nextId
      }
      ```
      
      Entity types: `line` {a,b}, `arc` {c,s,e}, `circle` {c,r}, `spline`
      {pts[], hs:{o[],i[]}, closed}, `text` {p0,pw,ph,text,font,weight,italic,
      tracking,leading,align,single,…}, `art` {p0,pw,ph,contours,closed,ratio}, and
      `part` — a rigid assembly body: `polylines` (the frozen master, one `[u,v]`
      polyline per contour in LOCAL mm), `pose` {tx,ty,rot} (world mm + degrees, the
      only thing that may change), `fixed` (Fix toggle: no solver variables at all),
      `grounded` + `groundAt` {u,v,wx,wy} (a marker pinned to the WORLD spot it
      occupied when it was grounded — never (0,0); rotation stays free), `width`
      (px), `color`, `name`. A part owns NO `state.points`; markers (every node +
      segment midpoint + a centroid for each closed loop) are derived from
      `polylines` at hit/draw time. `state.mates` = {id:
      {type:'pin'|'slider', a, aRef:{u,v}, b, bRef?, bEdge?{pl,i}}} joins two parts
      (grounding is the `grounded` flag above, not a mate row). Dragging a marker
      solves the whole assembly through `solveAssembly` in core.js (LM on the free
      poses, joint weight 100 : target weight 1, alternating target/repair passes,
      jitter escape only for parts that take part in the solve). Parts draw dark
      green (`#15803d`) in the light theme and light green (`#4ade80`) in the dark
      theme, never machine and never export (visualisation only).
      
      Part drag has **two personalities**, chosen at pointerdown:
      
      - **Free (no mate, not fixed): placement drag.** `t1` = the grabbed marker
        frozen at press; the snap cache (`partSnapCache()`: every visible point, plus
        midpoints and the origin) is built **once**; every frame the part is set to
        `startPose + (raw mouse delta)` and then shifted by `snap − wouldBeMarker`
        when a snap sits within 16 px (floor 2 mm) of where the grabbed marker would
        land. One calculation per frame from the start pose, so a caught snap stays
        caught until the mouse really leaves the radius.
      - **Mated / fixed: mechanism drag.** No snap, no bounded correction — the raw
        mouse position is the solver target each move (`{fast:true}`, warm start),
        and the release runs one full solve. Pressing the part's *body* (not a
        marker) drags 1:1 (mated parts solve, free parts translate).
      
      Multi-part selection drags as a group when no part in it is mated to a part
      outside the selection; Ctrl locks one axis; Ctrl+M moves the whole selection
      and its reference pick snaps to part markers too. A multi-point normal
      selection (a selected loop, several objects) body-drags with the same bounded
      snap as a free part (`selectionBodyDragFor`), excluding its own points from the
      cache.
      
      
      `text` extras: `leading` is line spacing in percent of the font size (default
      125, clamped 50–400) and `align` is `left|center|right`; both default to the old
      behaviour so older documents load unchanged. `single: true` marks a single-line
      (Hershey) font — that text has **no outlines**: `textStrokesWorld` returns open
      polylines and every consumer must keep `closed: false` (see `textOutlineWorld`).
      
      Constraint types: `coincident`, `distance` (also `kind:'radius'`),
      `horizontal`/`vertical` (per line), `horizontalPoints`/`verticalPoints`,
      `pointDim`, `pointOn`, `midpoint`, `tangent`, `tangentAt`, `parallel`,
      `perpendicular`, `equal`, `angle`, `aspect`, `fix`, `radius`.
      A dimension is a constraint with a `value`; `reference: true` means
      measure-only.
      
      `view` = `{ ox, oy, zoom }` (screen placement of the world).
      `ui` = everything transient (tool, selection, drag, drafts, panels).
      
      ## Invariants (each one caused a real bug — do not break them)
      
      1. **Spline handles are absolute world coordinates**, one entry per node in
         `hs.o` / `hs.i`; a `null` handle means a *corner* and the segment must still
         be drawn (straight). Never drop a segment because a handle is missing, and
         a **closed spline with exactly 2 nodes is a full loop** (both halves).
         When a node is removed, its handle entries must be removed with it: a
         pts/hs length mismatch silently replaces ALL handles with `autoHandles`
         approximations (that once made loop fills deviate from the outlines).
      2. **`art`/`text` contours are normalized 0..1 inside their frame** — round them
         with `round6`, never `round2`. World coordinates (mm) use `round2` on save.
      3. **Loop polygons hold coordinate copies**, never live `state.points`
         references — a live reference makes one vertex follow a later drag and the
         fill tears into a needle.
      4. **World is Y-up, canvas is Y-down** — convert only through `w2s`/`s2w`.
      5. **`invalidateLoops()` is the single "geometry changed" hook.** It drops the
         loop cache and the point-use index. Any code that adds/removes entities,
         rewires points **or moves spline handles** (they change the sampled curve)
         must call it (via `touch()`/`commit()`). While `ui.drag` is active the loop
         rebuild is deferred (`loopsDeferred`) to the first read after
         release — that is what keeps multi-thousand-point drags smooth.
      6. **`.sketch` format**: `version 2` packs points and handles as `[x, y]` at 2
         decimals; the loader still accepts the v1 `{x, y}` shape. Save/load
         round-trips must keep `closed` flags and null handles intact.
      7. **Editing affordances follow the active layer**: point markers, dimension
         labels and constraint badges draw only where they are grabbable
         (`pointEditable` / `constraintAnnotationActive`).
      8. **Loop fill may lag during a drag** and catches up on release (by design,
         see 5).
      9. **A framed object owns its guide lines.** `removeEntity` / `deleteSelection`
         must delete the text/picture's `guide` lines *and* every constraint that
         hangs off a point nothing else uses. A text's height dimension is a
         `distance` between `p0` and `ph`, not a constraint on the entity, so matching
         constraints by entity id alone leaves it behind after Delete.
      10. **A text font may arrive late.** Bundled families lazy-load a `FontFace`, so
         the outline trace cache keys on `FONT_EPOCH` (`fonts/fonts.js`) — never
         cache traced contours under a key that omits it, or the fallback-font outline
         survives the load.
      11. **Single-line fonts have no contours.** Anything that walks text outlines
          must go through `textOutlineWorld(e)` and respect its `closed` flag;
          `textContoursWorld` is empty for those fonts on purpose.
      12. **The curve fitter de-noises only what it recognises as a trace.** A dense
          wobbly contour (a traced glyph) is smoothed and resampled before fitting;
          a hand-drawn polyline is not. Corner detection measures direction over a
          window for the same reason. Do not lower that guard: smoothing a 4-point
          rectangle shaves its corners.
      13. **One snap switch, read everywhere.** `snapEnabled()` is `ui.snap !== ui.altDown`:
          Snap OFF means *nothing* snaps (points included — a dead snap used to look
          like a bug because endpoints still welded), and **Alt is its inverse while
          held**, so snap off + Alt borrows the snaps for a moment. `snapPoint`,
          `findSnapFor` and `partSnapCache` all gate on that one helper, so the
          preview, the hover marker and the click can never disagree. A part drag is
          not a snap magnet: the move is always the raw mouse delta and snap only
          *adds* a bounded correction, with a world floor (`max(2, 16/zoom)`) so deep
          zoom stays usable. A part's own baked source geometry still lives in
          `state.points` and shadows its outline — never exclude a whole bounding box
          of snaps, only points essentially coincident with the grab point.
      14. **The assembly solver never touches a spectator part.** Jitter escape for
          singular dead-points applies only to parts that carry a mate or a drag
          target; applying it to unconnected parts accumulates a free rotation each
          call and walks them off the screen. A `string` mate is display-only (a
          measuring thread, `len` recorded at creation, drawn grey as
          current-length + now/rest·100%): the solver has NO string residual — it
          never moves a part, and `partHasAnyMate` ignores it so a part hanging only
          on strings still drags 1:1 like a free part.
      15. **Mate picking is the one cross-layer exception.** While a mate job is
          open, `matePickable()` (visible + unlocked, any layer) replaces
          `entityEditable()` in the part hit-tests and `drawPartMarkers` shows every
          visible part's markers — an assembly spans layers. Everything else keeps
          the active-layer rule; locked still means locked even for a mate.
      
      ## Performance contracts
      
      - Never scan all entities per point (or vice versa). The point→entities index
        (`pointUses`) is the shared lookup; it registers **each entity once per
        point** (duplicates made handle-drag double-shift once). Same pattern for
        `selectionIndex()`.
      - `solveSketch` builds variables **only for points/radii the residuals touch**
        (recorded by a probe call). Adding "all points" back turns any solve into an
        O(n³) freeze.
      - `lmSolve` returns immediately when the initial cost is already ~0 — never
        remove that early-out (drag targets sit on the current positions).
      - `drawPoints` batches every marker into three `Path2D`s. Per-marker
        `beginPath` is what made thousand-point files crawl.
      - Autosave must never run for camera moves: pan/zoom write only the tiny
        `view` record (`minisketch.v1.view`); the document saves on real edits.
      
      ## Where to make changes
      
      | Goal | Where |
      | --- | --- |
      | New entity type | `entityPointIds`, draw branch in `drawEntities`, `cncPolyline`, `loadDocument`, `serializeState`, hit-testing (`entityScreenDistance`) |
      | New constraint type | residual in `solveSketch`, `constraintConflict`, badge/draw in `drawConstraintBadges`/`drawDimensions`, `loadDocument` |
      | New tool / shortcut | `onPointerDown` branch + `onKeyDown` switch + rail button + Help key table (both language panes!) |
      | New setting | `SETTINGS_SPEC` entry + `applySettings` |
      | New export format | mirror `downloadSketch` / `openSvgModal` |
      | Pure geometry/math | **`core.js` + a case in `tests/smoke.js`** |
      | Part / mate behaviour | `partTransform`, `partMarkersOf`, `partSnapCache`/`findSnapFor`, `solveAssemblyNow` (app.js); `solveAssembly` (core.js) + `testing/assembly_probe.js` |
      | New Tools-panel generator | **one new file in `tools/`** — see below |
      
      ## Tools-panel generators
      
      **Full guide: [`TOOLS.md`](TOOLS.md)** — the complete `api` reference (basic
      shapes, curves, constraints, offsets, document operations), a working example,
      the conventions, and how to test a tool.
      
      Each generator is its own file in `tools/` and registers itself with
      `tools/registry.js`:
      
      ```js
      window.MiniSketchTools.register({
        id: 'wall',            // also the gen.kind stored on the generated group
        label: 'Extrude wall', title: '…', modalId: 'wall-modal',
        modal: '<div id="wall-modal" …>…</div>',   // injected into <body> at mount
        open(api, params) {},   // fill the dialog (params = a re-edited group's gen)
        apply(api) {},          // generate; must end with a named group + gen.params
        wire() {}               // optional: extra dialog listeners
      });
      ```
      
      - `api` is the surface `toolApi()` in `app.js` exposes: model (`state`, `ui`,
        `settings`), helpers (`P`, `clamp`, `fmt`, `s2w`, `getW/getH`,
        `contentBounds`), shape builders (`addLine`, `addCircle`, `addArc`,
        `addSpline`, `addConstraint`), geometry (`bakeContours`, `offsetClosedChains`,
        `chainPolylines`, `clipperLib`, `signedAreaPts`, …) and document ops
        (`pushHistory`, `commit`, `toast`, `removeEntity`, `requestSolve`,
        `addPanelEntity`, `addPolylineEntity`, `cmdGroupSelection`). A tool must not
        reach into anything else.
      - Order matters only in `index.html`: `tools/registry.js`, then the tool files,
        then `core.js` and `app.js` (which calls `mountTools()` from `init()`). Because
        `core.js` loads *after* the tools, a tool must not call core helpers at module
        scope — only from inside `open` / `apply`.
      - Adding a tool needs no app.js edit: the registry appends its button to
        `#tools-row`, wires `.btn.primary` to `apply` and `[id$="-cancel"]` to close,
        and `openGeneratorDialog()` hands a double-clicked group to `reopen()`.
      - A generator must produce one named group with `gen = { kind: id, params }`,
        push history once (pass `{ noHistory: true }` to `cmdGroupSelection`), and
        keep its source geometry in `gen.params` so a re-edit never needs the
        originals. `node testing/tools_probe.js` enforces all of this for every file
        in `tools/` that registers itself.
      
      ## Testing
      
      See [`agents.md`](agents.md) — testing is the owner's job. The short version:
      
      - `node tests/smoke.js` must stay green — every entry there pins a bug that was
        actually shipped once (half-circles on import, dropped segments, solver
        freezes, winding direction).
      - The owner tests the app in a browser personally; describe what to check and
        what numbers to read (status bar `frame / draw ms`) instead of testing UI
        yourself.
      - When the owner reports a bug, fix it and hand it back for them to verify —
        never argue the report away. If it does not reproduce from reading the code,
        add a `console.log` of the real numbers and ask for the pasted output (or ask
        the owner to breakpoint it) instead of guessing.
      - If the owner proposes a fix, hear it first; disagree by discussing, not by
        silently replacing it.
      
      ## Known quirks
      
      - `normDeg` used to exist twice (fold-to-180 vs wrap-to-±180); the wrap version
        always won at runtime and is the one in `core.js`. The angle-violated check
        would prefer folding near ±180° — deliberate, unfixed.
      - `Ctrl+N` (Name selection) is reserved by Chrome; the panel button works.
      - Loop fills are intentionally stale while dragging (see invariant 5/8).
      
      ## The raster tracer
      
      `tools/trace.js` wraps the vendored `tools/imagetracer.js` (ImageTracerJS,
      **Unlicense / public domain**). It replaced `tools/Potrace.js`, which was GPL
      and would have forced the whole app to be GPL — the single blocker to shipping
      a closed-source product. Do not reintroduce a GPL library here.
      
      Two rules the wrapper enforces, both worth preserving:
      
      1. **Foreground only.** ImageTracerJS traces every palette colour, so the
         white background of a picture would come back as a rectangle spanning the
         whole sheet. `binarize()` turns the raster into black/white (Rec. 601 luma
         against `threshold`) and `trace()` keeps **only the dark layer**. A traced
         picture must never contain the background rectangle — the cutter would try
         to cut the whole sheet.
      2. **The preview is not the result.** The dialog draws a preview from a
         downscaled copy (320 px) so the tolerance can be tuned by watching it, but
         OK traces the **original pixels at full resolution**. Never make the
         preview the thing that gets inserted.
      
      `testing/trace_probe.js` pins both, plus the option mapping
      (`detail`→`ltres`, `curve`→`qtres`, `speckle`→`pathomit`, `blur`→`blurradius`,
      `corners`→`rightangleenhance`, `smooth`→`linefilter`).
      
      The trace dialog's knobs are read by `traceOptionsFromDialog()` in `app.js`;
      the preview is drawn by `drawTracePreview()` and re-drawn (debounced 180 ms)
      by `scheduleTracePreview()` whenever a knob changes.
      
      **The preview-affecting knobs are sliders with a number box beside them.**
      `bindTraceSlider(id, onChange)` keeps the two in step in both directions: the
      slider writes the exact value into the box, the box moves the slider (a value
      outside the slider's range pins it to the nearest end). The **number box is the
      value of record** — `traceOptionsFromDialog()` reads it, falling back to the
      slider when the box is empty. `setTraceValue(id, value, fallback)` puts a
      remembered value into both.
      
      **The settings are saved as they change**, not only when OK is pressed
      (`saveTracePrefs()`), so a tuning that was abandoned is still there the next
      time the panel opens. The saved object is merged into the existing
      `minisketch.v1.imgOpts` record, so the DPI and the mode survive alongside.
      
      **The preview shows what the import will produce.** `simplifyTracedPaths()`
      is shared by `insertArt()` and by the preview, and the preview's tolerance and
      minimum-area scale with its downscale factor — so the contour count under the
      preview is the count that will really land in the document, not the raw
      tracer's count.
      
      **The trace dialog has its own layout classes** — `trace-box` and
      `trace-opts` — and must not borrow `wide-cols`. Nine generator dialogs use
      `wide-cols` with the shared `.modal-cols .opt-col { width: 200px }`, and that
      rule has the higher specificity: a plain `.trace-opts { width: ... }` would
      lose to it and the panel would keep a 200px settings column with the sliders
      squashed and a hole beside them. `.modal-cols .opt-col.trace-opts` is
      deliberately more specific. `sizeTracePreview()` measures the settings column
      and gives the canvas that height, so the preview fills the column instead of
      leaving a hole under it; the canvas backing store is scaled by the device
      pixel ratio, so the outline stays sharp.

  content: |
      importScripts('geometry.js', 'nfp.js', 'nfp2.js', 'nfp_optimized.js', 'nfp_ga.js');
      
      // Handle messages from main thread
      self.onmessage = function (e) {
          const { parts, sheet, gridSize, algorithm, initialPlacements, gaParams, seedOrder } = e.data;
      
          // Create NFP instance based on algorithm
          let nfp;
          if (algorithm === 'nfp2') {
              nfp = new NFP2();
          } else if (algorithm === 'optimized') {
              nfp = new NFPOptimized();
          } else if (algorithm === 'ga') {
              nfp = new NFPGA();
              if (gaParams) nfp.setGAParams(gaParams.popSize, gaParams.generations, gaParams.mutationRate);
          } else {
              nfp = new NFP();
          }
          nfp.gridSize = gridSize;
      
          // Rehydrate initial placements
          const rehydratedInitial = (initialPlacements || []).map(plainPath => {
              const newPaths = plainPath.paths.map(p => p.map(pt => new Point(pt.x, pt.y)));
              const newPath = new Path(newPaths, plainPath.originIndex, plainPath.color, plainPath.lcolor);
              newPath.transformMatrix = plainPath.transformMatrix;
              newPath.childIndex = plainPath.childIndex;
              return newPath;
          });
      
          parts.forEach(part => {
              part.variants = part.variants.map(variant => {
                  const variantPath = new Path(
                      variant.paths,
                      variant.originIndex,
                      variant.color,
                      variant.lcolor
                  );
                  variantPath.childIndex = variant.childIndex;
                  variantPath.transformMatrix = variant.transformMatrix;
                  return variantPath;
              })
          });
      
          // Add progress handler
          const progressHandler = (placedCount, totalParts) => {
              self.postMessage({
                  type: 'progress',
                  progress: (placedCount / totalParts) * 100
              });
          };
      
          const bestPlacements = (algorithm === 'ga')
              ? nfp.findBestPosition(parts, sheet, progressHandler, gridSize, rehydratedInitial, seedOrder || null)
              : nfp.findBestPosition(parts, sheet, progressHandler, gridSize, rehydratedInitial);
      
          // Calculate total area for this solution
          const bounds = nfp.calculateTotalBounds(bestPlacements);
          const area = bounds.width * bounds.height;
      
          // Convert placements to transferable format
          const transferablePlacements = bestPlacements.map(part => {
              const result = {
                  paths: part.paths.map(p => p.map(pt => ({ x: pt.x, y: pt.y }))),
                  color: part.color,
                  lcolor: part.lcolor,
                  originIndex: part.originIndex,
                  childIndex: part.childIndex,
                  transformMatrix: [...part.transformMatrix]
              };
              return result;
          });
      
          // Send back final results
          self.postMessage({
              type: 'result',
              placements: transferablePlacements,
              area: area / (GEOM_SCALE * GEOM_SCALE),
              stats: nfp.getPerformanceStats(),
              bestOrder: nfp.bestOrder || null
          });
      };

  content: |
      /**
       * GA + NFP2 placement optimizer.
       *
       * Genetic Algorithm whose chromosome is ONLY the placement order
       * (a permutation of part indexes). The decoder is the existing,
       * unmodified NFP2.findBestNFPPlacement, called once per part in
       * chromosome order. Geometry, collision, offset, holes, export and
       * the worker protocol are untouched — this file only decides
       * "which part goes next".
       *
       * Fitness  = bounding-box area + total bbox area part yang tidak ternesting
       * (sisa besar = rugi bahan baru, sisa kecil masih bisa pakai bahan sisa).
       * Elitism always keeps the descending-size baseline individual, so a
       * GA run can never score worse than the plain heuristic order.
       */
      class NFPGA {
          constructor() {
              this.spacing = 0;
              this.allowFlip = true;
              this.gridSize = 10;
              this.performanceStats = {
                  generations: 0,
                  evaluations: 0,
                  collisionChecks: 0,
                  bestFitness: Infinity
              };
              // Last full-nest placements, reused as fixed obstacles during renest().
              this.lastPlacements = [];
              this.hascustomsheet = false;
              // GA hyper-parameters (defaults agreed with user).
              this.popSize = 6;
              this.generations = 5;
              this.mutationRate = 0.1;
          }
      
          setSpacing(spacing) {
              this.spacing = spacing * GEOM_SCALE;
              this.gridSize = spacing > 0 ? spacing * GEOM_SCALE : GEOM_SCALE;
          }
      
          setAllowFlip(allowFlip) { this.allowFlip = allowFlip; }
      
          setGAParams(popSize, generations, mutationRate) {
              if (popSize > 1) this.popSize = Math.floor(popSize);
              if (generations > 0) this.generations = Math.floor(generations);
              if (mutationRate >= 0 && mutationRate <= 1) this.mutationRate = mutationRate;
          }
      
          // ---- pure permutation helpers (no geometry here) ----
      
          _shuffled(n) {
              const a = [];
              for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) a.push(i);
              for (let i = n - 1; i > 0; i--) {
                  const j = (Math.random() * (i + 1)) | 0;
                  const t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t;
              }
              return a;
          }
      
          // Order crossover (OX): copy a slice of p1, fill the rest in p2 order.
          _crossover(p1, p2) {
              const n = p1.length;
              if (n < 2) return p1.slice();
              let a = (Math.random() * n) | 0;
              let b = (Math.random() * n) | 0;
              if (a > b) { const t = a; a = b; b = t; }
              const child = new Array(n).fill(-1);
              const used = new Set();
              for (let i = a; i <= b; i++) { child[i] = p1[i]; used.add(p1[i]); }
              let j = (b + 1) % n;
              for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                  const g = p2[(b + 1 + i) % n];
                  if (!used.has(g)) { child[j] = g; used.add(g); j = (j + 1) % n; }
              }
              return child;
          }
      
          // One random mutation of the placement order: swap two positions,
          // relocate one part, or invert a random segment.
          _mutateOrder(order) {
              const n = order.length;
              if (n < 2) return order;
              const a = order.slice();
              const r = Math.random();
              if (r < 0.5) {
                  const i = (Math.random() * n) | 0;
                  let j = (Math.random() * n) | 0;
                  if (i === j) j = (j + 1) % n;
                  const t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t;
              } else if (r < 0.8) {
                  const i = (Math.random() * n) | 0;
                  const g = a.splice(i, 1)[0];
                  a.splice((Math.random() * (n - 1 + 1)) | 0, 0, g);
              } else {
                  let i = (Math.random() * n) | 0;
                  let j = (Math.random() * n) | 0;
                  if (i > j) { const t = i; i = j; j = t; }
                  while (i < j) { const t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j] = t; i++; j--; }
              }
              return a;
          }
      
          // Random rotation-gene vector: one variant index per entry position.
          _randomRots() {
              return this._variantCounts.map(c => (Math.random() * c) | 0);
          }
      
          // Uniform crossover of two rotation vectors.
          _crossoverRots(r1, r2) {
              const n = r1.length;
              const child = new Array(n);
              for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) child[i] = Math.random() < 0.5 ? r1[i] : r2[i];
              return child;
          }
      
          // Mutate one individual ({order, rots}): always shuffle the order a
          // little (SVGnest-style, keeps every generation exploring), and with
          // probability mutationRate also change one rotation gene.
          _mutate(ind) {
              const order = this._mutateOrder(ind.order);
              let rots = ind.rots;
              if (Math.random() < this.mutationRate) {
                  rots = ind.rots.slice();
                  const i = (Math.random() * rots.length) | 0;
                  const c = this._variantCounts[i];
                  if (c > 1) {
                      let v = (Math.random() * c) | 0;
                      if (v === rots[i]) v = (v + 1) % c;
                      rots[i] = v;
                  }
              }
              return { order, rots };
          }
      
          // A seed from the previous infinite-loop iteration is valid only when
          // it is a full permutation of the current entry positions.
          _isValidSeed(seed, n) {
              if (!seed || !Array.isArray(seed.order) || !Array.isArray(seed.rots)) return false;
              if (seed.order.length !== n || seed.rots.length !== n) return false;
              const seen = new Array(n).fill(false);
              for (const v of seed.order) {
                  if (!Number.isInteger(v) || v < 0 || v >= n || seen[v]) return false;
                  seen[v] = true;
              }
              return true;
          }
      
          _tournament(fits, k) {
              let best = (Math.random() * fits.length) | 0;
              for (let i = 1; i < k; i++) {
                  const c = (Math.random() * fits.length) | 0;
                  if (fits[c] < fits[best]) best = c;
              }
              return best;
          }
      
          /**
           * Bounding-box area of one entry (variant 0, scaled units).
           * Cached per entry object so the fitness loop stays cheap.
           */
          _entryArea(e) {
              if (e._gaArea !== undefined) return e._gaArea;
              let a = 0;
              if (e.variants && e.variants.length > 0) {
                  const b = e.variants[0].getBounds();
                  a = b.width * b.height;
              }
              e._gaArea = a;
              return a;
          }
      
          /**
           * Decode one chromosome: place parts in `order` using a fresh,
           * unmodified NFP2 instance as the decoder. Rotation genes pick one
           * variant per part (SVGnest-style); order-only entries fall back to
           * trying all variants so old seeds stay valid.
           * Fitness = bounding-box area + total bbox area yang tidak ternesting.
           * Jadi GA memprioritaskan part BESAR lebih dulu: sisa besar = rugi bahan
           * baru, sisa kecil masih bisa pakai bahan sisa.
           * ctx = { entries, scaledSheet, gridSize, stats }
           * Returns { placements, fitness, unplaced, unplacedArea }.
           */
          _evaluate(ind, ctx) {
              const order = Array.isArray(ind) ? ind : ind.order;
              const dec = new NFP2();
              dec.spacing = this.spacing;
              dec.allowFlip = this.allowFlip;
              dec.gridSize = this.gridSize;
              dec.performanceStats = { boundaryPointsTested: 0, collisionAvoided: 0, collisionChecks: 0 };
              const cellSize = Math.max(50 * GEOM_SCALE, ctx.gridSize * 5);
              dec.spatialHash = new NFP2SpatialHash(cellSize);
      
              const sheet = { width: ctx.scaledSheet.width, height: ctx.scaledSheet.height };
              const placed = ctx.fixed.slice();
              for (const p of placed) dec.spatialHash.add(p);
      
              // Custom sheet outlines (green) become the sheet, exactly like NFP2.
              for (const e of ctx.entries) {
                  if (e.lcolor !== '#00ff00') continue;
                  const sv = e.variants[0];
                  sv.align();
                  const b = sv.getBounds();
                  sheet.width = b.width;
                  sheet.height = b.height;
                  dec.hascustomsheet = true;
                  const c = sv.clone();
                  c.childIndex = e.childIndex;
                  placed.push(c);
                  dec.spatialHash.add(c);
              }
      
              let unplaced = 0;
              let unplacedArea = 0;
              for (let k = 0; k < order.length; k++) {
                  const e = ctx.entries[order[k]];
                  if (!e || ctx.initialSet.has(e.originIndex)) continue;
                  if (e.lcolor === '#00ff00') continue; // fixed by decoder above
                  let bp = null;
                  if (ind && !Array.isArray(ind) && ind.rots) {
                      bp = this._placeWithVariant(dec, e, ind.rots[order[k]], placed, sheet, ctx.gridSize);
                  } else {
                      bp = dec.findBestNFPPlacement(e, placed, sheet, ctx.gridSize);
                  }
                  if (bp) {
                      bp.childIndex = e.childIndex;
                      placed.push(bp);
                      dec.spatialHash.add(bp);
                  } else {
                      unplaced++;
                      unplacedArea += this._entryArea(e);
                  }
              }
      
              let area = 0;
              if (placed.length > 0) {
                  const b = dec.calculateTotalBounds(placed);
                  area = b.width * b.height;
              }
              ctx.stats.collisionChecks += dec.performanceStats.collisionChecks || 0;
              return { placements: placed, fitness: area + unplacedArea, unplaced: unplaced, unplacedArea: unplacedArea };
          }
      
          /**
           * Place one part trying only the rotation gene (a single variant
           * index), mirroring SVGnest where the genome carries rotation.
           * Falls back to all variants when the gene is missing or invalid
           * (multi-flip variants generate extra indices at runtime).
           */
          _placeWithVariant(dec, entry, gene, placed, sheet, gridSize) {
              const variants = entry.variants;
              if (!variants || variants.length === 0) return null;
              let list = variants;
              if (Number.isInteger(gene)) {
                  const v = variants[((gene % variants.length) + variants.length) % variants.length];
                  if (v) list = [v];
              }
              const single = { variants: list, childIndex: entry.childIndex };
              return dec.findBestNFPPlacement(single, placed, sheet, gridSize);
          }
      
          findBestPosition(parts, sheet, progressHandler, gridSize, initialPlacements = [], seedOrder = null) {
              const startTime = performance.now();
              const scaledSheet = {
                  width: sheet.width * GEOM_SCALE,
                  height: sheet.height * GEOM_SCALE
              };
              this.hascustomsheet = false;
      
              // Full nest clears all placement flags, like NFP2.
              parts.forEach(p => { p.placed = false; });
      
              const initialSet = new Set(initialPlacements.map(p => p.originIndex));
              const entries = parts
                  .map((p, i) => ({ part: p, idx: i }))
                  .filter(e => !initialSet.has(e.part.originIndex));
              const placeables = entries.filter(e => e.part.lcolor !== '#00ff00');
      
              // Degenerate case: nothing to order, keep NFP2 behaviour.
              if (placeables.length === 0) {
                  const dec = new NFP2();
                  dec.spacing = this.spacing;
                  dec.allowFlip = this.allowFlip;
                  dec.gridSize = gridSize;
                  const out = dec.findBestPosition(parts, sheet, progressHandler, gridSize, initialPlacements);
                  this.lastPlacements = dec.lastPlacements;
                  this.hascustomsheet = dec.hascustomsheet;
                  this.performanceStats = {
                      generations: 0, evaluations: 1,
                      collisionChecks: (dec.performanceStats && dec.performanceStats.collisionChecks) || 0,
                      bestFitness: Infinity
                  };
                  return out;
              }
      
              // Baseline individual: descending size (longest side squared),
              // same metric NFP2 uses for its passes. Elitism keeps it, so the
              // GA result is never worse than this heuristic order.
              const sizeOf = (w) => {
                  const b = w.part.variants[0].getBounds();
                  const l = Math.max(b.width, b.height);
                  return l * l;
              };
              // Custom-sheet (green) entries are fixed by the decoder, so they are
              // excluded from the chromosome; only placeable parts are ordered.
              const baselineOrder = placeables
                  .map(e => entries.indexOf(e))
                  .sort((a, b) => sizeOf(entries[b]) - sizeOf(entries[a]));
      
              const ctx = {
                  entries: entries.map(e => e.part),
                  scaledSheet: scaledSheet,
                  gridSize: gridSize,
                  fixed: initialPlacements.slice(),
                  initialSet: initialSet,
                  stats: { collisionChecks: 0 }
              };
      
              // Variant counts per entry position (one rotation gene each).
              // Flip adds its own variant indices on top of rotation, so counts
              // are read live from the entries.
              this._variantCounts = ctx.entries.map(e =>
                  (e.variants && e.variants.length > 0) ? e.variants.length : 1);
      
              const popSize = Math.max(2, this.popSize);
              // Chromosome = permutation of ENTRY positions (0..entries.length-1),
              // so duplicate parts stay distinguishable.
              const n = entries.length;
              const baseSet = new Set(baselineOrder);
              // Full permutation of all entry positions; the fixed green entries
              // simply decode to no-ops wherever they appear in the order.
              // The first individual keeps the heuristic solution up front
              // (baseline positions first) so elitism can never lose it.
              const baseRots = this._randomRots();
              let pop = [{ order: baselineOrder.concat(
                  Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => i).filter(i => !baseSet.has(i))
              ), rots: baseRots }];
              // Individual #2 continues the winner of the previous infinite-loop
              // iteration (mutated fresh each loop so exploration never stalls).
              if (this._isValidSeed(seedOrder, n)) {
                  pop.push({ order: seedOrder.order.slice(), rots: seedOrder.rots.slice() });
              }
              while (pop.length < popSize) pop.push({ order: this._shuffled(n), rots: this._randomRots() });
      
              const totalEvals = pop.length * Math.max(1, this.generations) + 1;
              let evalsDone = 0;
              let fits = pop.map(o => {
                  const r = this._evaluate(o, ctx);
                  if (progressHandler) progressHandler(++evalsDone, totalEvals);
                  return r.fitness;
              });
      
              const ELITES = Math.min(2, pop.length);
              for (let g = 0; g < this.generations; g++) {
                  const ranked = pop.map((o, i) => i).sort((a, b) => fits[a] - fits[b]);
                  const next = [];
                  for (let e = 0; e < ELITES; e++) next.push(pop[ranked[e]]);
                  while (next.length < pop.length) {
                      const p1 = pop[this._tournament(fits, 3)];
                      const p2 = pop[this._tournament(fits, 3)];
                      const order = this._crossover(p1.order, p2.order);
                      const rots = this._crossoverRots(p1.rots, p2.rots);
                      next.push(this._mutate({ order, rots }));
                  }
                  pop = next;
                  fits = pop.map((o, i) => {
                      // Elites carry their fitness over without re-evaluation.
                      if (i < ELITES) return fits[ranked[i]];
                      const r = this._evaluate(o, ctx);
                      if (progressHandler) progressHandler(++evalsDone, totalEvals);
                      return r.fitness;
                  });
              }
      
              const ranked = pop.map((o, i) => i).sort((a, b) => fits[a] - fits[b]);
              const bestInd = pop[ranked[0]];
              const best = this._evaluate(bestInd, ctx);
              if (progressHandler) progressHandler(++evalsDone, totalEvals);
      
              this.performanceStats = {
                  generations: this.generations,
                  evaluations: evalsDone,
                  collisionChecks: ctx.stats.collisionChecks,
                  bestFitness: best.fitness
              };
              this.lastPlacements = best.placements;
              // Winner chromosome for the next infinite-loop iteration.
              this.bestOrder = { order: bestInd.order.slice(), rots: bestInd.rots.slice() };
      
              const endTime = performance.now();
              console.log('NFP-GA Performance:', {
                  time: ((endTime - startTime).toFixed(2) + 'ms'),
                  partsProcessed: parts.length,
                  unplaced: best.unplaced,
                  unplacedArea: (best.unplacedArea / (GEOM_SCALE * GEOM_SCALE)).toFixed(2) + ' mm²',
                  bestFitness: best.fitness / (GEOM_SCALE * GEOM_SCALE),
                  ...this.performanceStats
              });
      
              return best.placements;
          }
      
          // Partial renesting and compaction reuse the proven NFP2 code paths
          // unchanged; only the full-nest search is genetic.
          renest(parts, sheet, progressHandler, gridSize) {
              const dec = new NFP2();
              dec.spacing = this.spacing;
              dec.allowFlip = this.allowFlip;
              dec.gridSize = this.gridSize;
              dec.lastPlacements = this.lastPlacements;
              const out = dec.renest(parts, sheet, progressHandler, gridSize);
              this.lastPlacements = dec.lastPlacements;
              return out;
          }
      
          compactSolution(placements, sheet) {
              const dec = new NFP2();
              dec.spacing = this.spacing;
              dec.allowFlip = this.allowFlip;
              dec.gridSize = this.gridSize;
              return dec.compactSolution(placements, sheet);
          }
      
          checkDragPlacement(part, x, y, placedParts, sheet) {
              const dec = new NFP2();
              return dec.checkDragPlacement(part, x, y, placedParts, sheet);
          }
      
          calculateTotalBounds(parts) {
              if (parts.length === 0) return { x: 0, y: 0, width: 10, height: 10 };
              let minX = Infinity, minY = Infinity, maxX = -Infinity, maxY = -Infinity;
              for (const part of parts) {
                  if (part.lcolor === '#00ff00') continue;
                  const b = part.getBounds();
                  minX = Math.min(minX, b.x);
                  minY = Math.min(minY, b.y);
                  maxX = Math.max(maxX, b.x + b.width);
                  maxY = Math.max(maxY, b.y + b.height);
              }
              return { x: minX, y: minY, width: maxX - minX, height: maxY - minY };
          }
      
          getPerformanceStats() { return this.performanceStats; }
      }

      /**
       * True NFP (No-Fit Polygon) Algorithm Implementation
       * This provides proper geometric placement using NFP boundary sampling
       * instead of brute force collision detection
       */
      
      class NFP2SpatialHash {
          constructor(cellSize) {
              this.cellSize = cellSize;
              this.grid = new Map();
              this.queryId = 0;
              this.resultArray = [];
          }
      
          add(part) {
              const bounds = part.getBounds();
              const startX = Math.floor(bounds.x / this.cellSize);
              const endX = Math.floor((bounds.x + bounds.width) / this.cellSize);
              const startY = Math.floor(bounds.y / this.cellSize);
              const endY = Math.floor((bounds.y + bounds.height) / this.cellSize);
      
              for (let x = startX; x <= endX; x++) {
                  for (let y = startY; y <= endY; y++) {
                      const key = (x << 16) | (y & 0xFFFF);
                      if (!this.grid.has(key)) {
                          this.grid.set(key, []);
                      }
                      this.grid.get(key).push(part);
                  }
              }
          }
      
          remove(part) {
              const bounds = part.getBounds();
              const startX = Math.floor(bounds.x / this.cellSize);
              const endX = Math.floor((bounds.x + bounds.width) / this.cellSize);
              const startY = Math.floor(bounds.y / this.cellSize);
              const endY = Math.floor((bounds.y + bounds.height) / this.cellSize);
      
              for (let x = startX; x <= endX; x++) {
                  for (let y = startY; y <= endY; y++) {
                      const key = (x << 16) | (y & 0xFFFF);
                      const cell = this.grid.get(key);
                      if (cell) {
                          const idx = cell.indexOf(part);
                          if (idx !== -1) cell.splice(idx, 1);
                      }
                  }
              }
          }
      
          // Returns a REUSABLE array (deduped via queryId stamping) — the caller must
          // consume it before the next query. Parts may span several cells, so a part
          // appears in multiple cells; the stamping avoids pushing it more than once.
          query(bx, by, bw, bh) {
              const startX = Math.floor(bx / this.cellSize);
              const endX = Math.floor((bx + bw) / this.cellSize);
              const startY = Math.floor(by / this.cellSize);
              const endY = Math.floor((by + bh) / this.cellSize);
      
              const results = this.resultArray;
              results.length = 0;
              const qId = ++this.queryId;
      
              for (let x = startX; x <= endX; x++) {
                  for (let y = startY; y <= endY; y++) {
                      const key = (x << 16) | (y & 0xFFFF);
                      const cell = this.grid.get(key);
                      if (cell) {
                          const cellLen = cell.length;
                          for (let i = 0; i < cellLen; i++) {
                              const part = cell[i];
                              if (part._lastQueryId !== qId) {
                                  part._lastQueryId = qId;
                                  results.push(part);
                              }
                          }
                      }
                  }
              }
              return results;
          }
      }
      
      class NFP2 {
          constructor() {
              this.spacing = 0;
              this.allowFlip = true;
              this.performanceStats = {
                  boundaryPointsTested: 0,
                  collisionAvoided: 0,
                  collisionChecks: 0
              };
              this.spatialHash = null;
              this.gridSize = 10;
              // Last full-nest placements, reused as fixed obstacles during renest().
              this.lastPlacements = [];
          }
      
          setSpacing(spacing) {
              this.spacing = spacing * GEOM_SCALE;
              this.gridSize = spacing > 0 ? spacing * GEOM_SCALE : GEOM_SCALE;
          }
          setAllowFlip(allowFlip) { this.allowFlip = allowFlip; }
      
          findBestPosition(parts, sheet, progressHandler, gridSize, initialPlacements = []) {
              const startTime = performance.now();
              // gridSize is already scaled
              const scaledGridSize = gridSize;
              const scaledSheet = {
                  width: sheet.width * GEOM_SCALE,
                  height: sheet.height * GEOM_SCALE
              };
              this.performanceStats = {
                  boundaryPointsTested: 0,
                  collisionAvoided: 0,
                  collisionChecks: 0
              };
      
              // Set of originIndexes already fixed as initial placements (renesting).
              // These must NOT be re-placed, otherwise they would appear twice.
              this._initialIndexSet = initialPlacements.length > 0
                  ? new Set(initialPlacements.map(p => p.originIndex))
                  : null;
      
              const cellSize = Math.max(50 * GEOM_SCALE, scaledGridSize * 5);
              this.spatialHash = new NFP2SpatialHash(cellSize);
      
              let bestPlacementsAll = [...initialPlacements];
              // Add initial placements to spatial hash
              initialPlacements.forEach(p => this.spatialHash.add(p));
      
              const totalParts = parts.length;
              this.hascustomsheet = false;
      
              // Full nest (Start nesting) clears all placement flags.
              parts.forEach(p => { p.placed = false; });
      
              // Run the shared placement loop (also used by renest()).
              this._runPlacementPasses(parts, bestPlacementsAll, scaledSheet, scaledGridSize, progressHandler, totalParts);
      
              const endTime = performance.now();
              console.log(`NFP2 Performance:`, {
                  time: `${(endTime - startTime).toFixed(2)}ms`,
                  partsProcessed: totalParts,
                  ...this.performanceStats
              });
      
              this.lastPlacements = bestPlacementsAll;
              return bestPlacementsAll;
          }
      
          /**
           * Shared core placement loop. Places every part in `parts` whose `placed`
           * flag is false, using the already-placed parts and the seeded spatial hash
           * as fixed obstacles. Used by both findBestPosition (full nest) and
           * renest() (partial re-placement of marked parts).
           *
           * NOTE: this method intentionally does NOT reset part.placed flags. The
           * caller decides which parts should be re-placed (placed=false).
           */
          _runPlacementPasses(parts, bestPlacementsAll, scaledSheet, scaledGridSize, progressHandler, totalParts) {
              const partData = new Map();
              let maxArea = 0, minArea = Infinity;
      
              for (const part of parts) {
                  // Fixed (already placed) parts act as obstacles; skip them here.
                  if (part.placed) continue;
                  // Parts fixed as initial placements should not be re-placed.
                  if (this._initialIndexSet && this._initialIndexSet.has(part.originIndex)) {
                      part.placed = true;
                      continue;
                  }
                  if (part.lcolor === "#00ff00") {
                      const sheetVariant = part.variants[0];
                      sheetVariant.align();
                      const bounds = sheetVariant.getBounds();
                      scaledSheet.width = bounds.width;
                      scaledSheet.height = bounds.height;
                      this.hascustomsheet = true;
                      const placedSheet = sheetVariant.clone();
                      bestPlacementsAll.push(placedSheet);
                      this.spatialHash.add(placedSheet);
                      part.placed = true;
                      continue;
                  }
                  const b = part.variants[0].getBounds();
                  const longestSide = Math.max(b.width, b.height);
                  const area = longestSide * longestSide;
                  partData.set(part, { area, aspectRatio: b.width / b.height });
                  maxArea = Math.max(maxArea, area);
                  minArea = Math.min(minArea, area);
              }
      
              const remainingParts = parts.filter(part => !part.placed && part.lcolor !== "#00ff00");
              const areaRange = maxArea - minArea;
              const thresholds = [
                  minArea + areaRange * 0.75,
                  minArea + areaRange * 0.5,
                  minArea + areaRange * 0.25,
                  minArea
              ];
      
              // Process in 4 passes like nfp.js to ensure large parts are prioritized.
              for (let pass = 0; pass < 4; pass++) {
                  const passParts = remainingParts.filter(part => {
                      if (part.placed) return false;
                      const area = partData.get(part).area;
                      if (pass === 0) return area >= thresholds[0];
                      if (pass === 1) return area >= thresholds[1];
                      if (pass === 2) return area >= thresholds[2];
                      return true;
                  });
      
                  passParts.sort((a, b) => {
                      const aD = partData.get(a);
                      const bD = partData.get(b);
                      const scoreA = aD.area * Math.abs(1 - aD.aspectRatio);
                      const scoreB = bD.area * Math.abs(1 - bD.aspectRatio);
                      const noise = (Math.random() - 0.5) * (scoreA + scoreB) * 0.1;
                      return scoreB - scoreA + noise;
                  });
      
                  for (let part of passParts) {
                      if (part.placed) continue;
                      const bestPlacement = this.findBestNFPPlacement(part, bestPlacementsAll, scaledSheet, scaledGridSize);
                      if (bestPlacement) {
                          bestPlacement.childIndex = part.childIndex;
                          bestPlacementsAll.push(bestPlacement);
                          this.spatialHash.add(bestPlacement);
                          part.placed = true;
                      }
                      if (progressHandler) progressHandler(bestPlacementsAll.length, totalParts);
                  }
              }
          }
      
          /**
           * Partial re-nesting: re-place only the parts whose `placed` flag is false,
           * using the last full-nest result (this.lastPlacements) as fixed obstacles.
           * Does NOT reset part positions — the caller marks exactly the parts to move.
           */
          renest(parts, sheet, progressHandler, gridSize) {
              const startTime = performance.now();
              const scaledGridSize = gridSize;
              const scaledSheet = {
                  width: sheet.width * GEOM_SCALE,
                  height: sheet.height * GEOM_SCALE
              };
              const totalParts = parts.length;
      
              const markedSet = new Set();
              for (const p of parts) {
                  if (p.placed === false) markedSet.add(p.originIndex);
              }
      
              const fixedPlacements = (this.lastPlacements || []).filter(p => !markedSet.has(p.originIndex));
      
              this.performanceStats = { boundaryPointsTested: 0, collisionAvoided: 0, collisionChecks: 0 };
              this._initialIndexSet = new Set(fixedPlacements.map(p => p.originIndex));
      
              const cellSize = Math.max(50 * GEOM_SCALE, scaledGridSize * 5);
              this.spatialHash = new NFP2SpatialHash(cellSize);
              fixedPlacements.forEach(p => this.spatialHash.add(p));
      
              for (const p of fixedPlacements) {
                  if (p.lcolor === "#00ff00") {
                      const b = p.getBounds();
                      scaledSheet.width = b.width;
                      scaledSheet.height = b.height;
                      this.hascustomsheet = true;
                      break;
                  }
              }
      
              const bestPlacementsAll = fixedPlacements.slice();
              this._runPlacementPasses(parts, bestPlacementsAll, scaledSheet, scaledGridSize, progressHandler, totalParts);
      
              const endTime = performance.now();
              console.log(`NFP2 Renest Performance:`, {
                  time: `${(endTime - startTime).toFixed(2)}ms`,
                  partsProcessed: totalParts,
                  rePlaced: markedSet.size,
                  ...this.performanceStats
              });
      
              this.lastPlacements = bestPlacementsAll;
              return bestPlacementsAll;
          }
      
          findBestNFPPlacement(part, placedPartsAll, sheet, gridSize) {
              const sheetParts = placedPartsAll.filter(p => p.lcolor === "#00ff00");
              let bestPlacement = null;
              let bestScore = Infinity;
      
              // 1. Scanline-based search (The Speed/Compactness from nfp.js)
              // gridSize is already scaled
              const yStep = Math.max(4 * GEOM_SCALE, gridSize);
              const xStep = Math.max(4 * GEOM_SCALE, gridSize);
      
              // Precompute each placed part's vertical span once, so the scanline
              // loop can skip parts that cannot cross the current y without calling
              // getBounds() (or getHorizontalIntersections) for every scanline.
              const scanParts = placedPartsAll.map(p => {
                  const b = p.getBounds();
                  return { p, minY: b.y, maxY: b.y + b.height };
              });
      
              for (let y = 0; y < sheet.height; y += yStep) {
                  const intersections = [];
                  let sheetRange = [0, sheet.width];
      
                  for (const sp of scanParts) {
                      if (y < sp.minY || y > sp.maxY) continue;
                      const placed = sp.p;
                      const pts = GeometryUtil.getHorizontalIntersections(placed, y);
                      if (placed.lcolor === "#00ff00") {
                          if (pts.length >= 2) {
                              pts.sort((a, b) => a - b);
                              sheetRange = [pts[0], pts[pts.length - 1]];
                          }
                      } else {
                          intersections.push(...pts);
                      }
                  }
                  intersections.sort((a, b) => a - b);
      
                  for (let x = sheetRange[0]; x <= sheetRange[1]; x += xStep) {
                      let insideAnyPart = false;
                      for (let i = 0; i < intersections.length; i += 2) {
                          if (x >= intersections[i] && x <= intersections[i + 1]) {
                              x = Math.ceil(intersections[i + 1]);
                              insideAnyPart = true;
                              break;
                          }
                      }
                      if (insideAnyPart) continue;
      
                      for (let variant of part.variants) {
                          const b = variant.getBounds();
                          const dx = x - b.x;
                          const dy = y - b.y;
      
                          if (x < 0 || y < 0 || x + b.width > sheet.width || y + b.height > sheet.height) continue;
      
                          const score = (y + b.height * 2) * 2 + (x * 0.1) + (variant.paths.length > 1 ? 1000 * GEOM_SCALE : 0);
                          if (score > bestScore + 100) continue;
      
                          variant.insideBonus = 0;
                          if (!this.checkCollisions(variant, dx, dy, sheetParts)) {
                              const finalScore = score - (variant.insideBonus || 0);
                              if (finalScore < bestScore) {
                                  bestScore = finalScore;
                                  bestPlacement = variant.clone(dx, dy);
                                  if (variant.insideBonus > 5000) return bestPlacement;
                              }
                          }
                      }
                  }
                  // Stop evaluation if we have a very solid result at the top
                  if (bestPlacement && y > sheet.height / 3) break;
              }
      
              // 2. Vertex Refinement (The Precision from NFP)
              // If we haven't found a perfect top spot, try one fast pass through NFP vertices
              if (!bestPlacement || bestScore > (sheet.height * 0.5)) {
                  const edgeCandidates = this.getCandidatePositions(part.variants[0], placedPartsAll, sheet, gridSize);
                  for (let pos of edgeCandidates) {
                      const b = part.variants[0].getBounds();
                      const score = ((pos.y + b.y) + b.height * 2) * 2 + ((pos.x + b.x) * 0.1);
                      if (score < bestScore) {
                          if (!this.checkCollisions(part.variants[0], pos.x, pos.y, sheetParts)) {
                              bestPlacement = part.variants[0].clone(pos.x, pos.y);
                              bestScore = score;
                          }
                      }
                  }
              }
      
              return bestPlacement;
          }
      
          getCandidatePositions(part, placedParts, sheet, gridSize) {
              const positions = [];
              const pb = part.getBounds();
              const pW = pb.width;
              const pH = pb.height;
      
              // 1. Initial start points along the top and left to encourage top-left packing
              const startStep = gridSize * 2;
              for (let x = 0; x <= sheet.width; x += startStep) {
                  positions.push({ x: x - pb.x, y: -pb.y });
              }
              for (let y = 0; y <= sheet.height / 2; y += startStep) {
                  positions.push({ x: -pb.x, y: y - pb.y });
              }
      
              if (placedParts.length === 0) return positions;
      
              const seen = new Set();
              const addPos = (x, y) => {
                  const k = `${Math.round(x)},${Math.round(y)}`;
                  if (!seen.has(k)) {
                      positions.push({ x, y });
                      seen.add(k);
                  }
              };
      
              // Pre-sample vertices from the new part to try vertex-to-vertex alignment
              const newPartPath = part.paths[0];
              const vSamples = [];
      
              // Use corners + center-edge points. Add more for "Maximum Packing" mode.
              vSamples.push({ x: pb.x, y: pb.y });
              vSamples.push({ x: pb.x + pW, y: pb.y });
              vSamples.push({ x: pb.x + pW, y: pb.y + pH });
              vSamples.push({ x: pb.x, y: pb.y + pH });
              vSamples.push({ x: pb.x + pW / 2, y: pb.y });
              vSamples.push({ x: pb.x, y: pb.y + pH / 2 });
      
              if (this.gridSize < 3) {
                  // Maximum Packing: add more mid-points
                  vSamples.push({ x: pb.x + pW / 2, y: pb.y + pH });
                  vSamples.push({ x: pb.x + pW, y: pb.y + pH / 2 });
                  vSamples.push({ x: pb.x + pW / 2, y: pb.y + pH / 2 });
              }
      
              for (const placed of placedParts) {
                  if (placed.lcolor === "#00ff00") continue; // Sheets handled by scanline
      
                  for (const path of placed.paths) {
                      const len = path.length;
                      if (len < 2) continue;
      
                      // Dynamic vertex sampling based on gridSize (Smaller = More Precise)
                      const vSkip = Math.max(1, Math.floor(gridSize / (2 * GEOM_SCALE)));
                      for (let i = 0; i < len; i += vSkip) {
                          const pt = path[i];
                          for (const v of vSamples) {
                              addPos(pt.x - v.x, pt.y - v.y);
                          }
                      }
                  }
              }
      
              return positions.filter(p => {
                  const bx = p.x + pb.x;
                  const by = p.y + pb.y;
                  return bx >= 0 && bx + pb.width <= sheet.width &&
                      by >= 0 && by + pb.height <= sheet.height;
              });
          }
      
          checkCollisions(variant, dx, dy, sheetParts) {
              const vBounds = variant.getBounds();
              const bx = vBounds.x + dx;
              const by = vBounds.y + dy;
              const bw = vBounds.width;
              const bh = vBounds.height;
      
              // 1. Sheet constraints
              for (const s of sheetParts) {
                  this.performanceStats.collisionChecks++;
                  if (GeometryUtil.polyOutsideAt(variant, dx, dy, s)) return true;
              }
      
              const candidates = this.spatialHash.query(bx, by, bw, bh);
      
              // Note: initial/fixed placements are always seeded into the spatial
              // hash, and overlapping bboxes provably share a grid cell, so the
              // hash query already returns every relevant placed part.
      
              // 2. Part intersections
              for (const placed of candidates) {
                  if (placed.lcolor === "#00ff00") continue;
      
                  const pb = placed._cachedBounds || placed.getBounds();
                  if (bx > pb.x + pb.width || bx + bw < pb.x ||
                      by > pb.y + pb.height || by + bh < pb.y) {
                      continue;
                  }
      
                  this.performanceStats.collisionChecks++;
                  if (GeometryUtil.polygonsIntersectAt(variant, dx, dy, placed, true)) return true;
              }
      
              return false;
          }
      
          calculateTotalBounds(parts) {
              if (parts.length === 0) return { x: 0, y: 0, width: 10, height: 10 };
              let minX = Infinity, minY = Infinity, maxX = -Infinity, maxY = -Infinity;
              for (const part of parts) {
                  if (part.lcolor === "#00ff00") continue;
                  const b = part.getBounds();
                  minX = Math.min(minX, b.x);
                  minY = Math.min(minY, b.y);
                  maxX = Math.max(maxX, b.x + b.width);
                  maxY = Math.max(maxY, b.y + b.height);
              }
              return { x: minX, y: minY, width: maxX - minX, height: maxY - minY };
          }
      
          getPerformanceStats() { return this.performanceStats; }
      
          compactSolution(placements, sheet) {
              const cellSize = (this.spatialHash && this.spatialHash.cellSize) ||
                  Math.max(50 * GEOM_SCALE, (this.gridSize || 10) * 5);
              this.spatialHash = new NFP2SpatialHash(cellSize);
              placements.forEach(p => this.spatialHash.add(p));
              const sheetParts = placements.filter(p => p.lcolor === "#00ff00");
      
              const collisionCheck = (part, phase) => {
                  if (part.lcolor === "#00ff00") return false;
      
                  if (phase === 'start') {
                      this.spatialHash.remove(part);
                      return false;
                  }
                  if (phase === 'end') {
                      this.spatialHash.add(part);
                      return false;
                  }
      
                  const b = part.getBounds();
                  if (b.x < 0 || b.y < 0 || b.x + b.width > sheet.width * GEOM_SCALE || b.y + b.height > sheet.height * GEOM_SCALE) {
                      return true;
                  }
      
                  return this.checkCollisions(part, 0, 0, sheetParts);
              };
      
              const moves = GeometryUtil.compactLayout(placements, collisionCheck);
              console.log(`NFP2 Compaction done. Multi-pass moves: ${moves}`);
              return placements;
          }
      
          checkDragPlacement(part, x, y, placedParts, sheet) {
              const scaledSheet = {
                  width: sheet.width * GEOM_SCALE,
                  height: sheet.height * GEOM_SCALE
              };
      
              const bounds = part.getBounds();
              const bx = bounds.x;
              const by = bounds.y;
              const bw = bounds.width;
              const bh = bounds.height;
      
              // Check sheet boundaries with small epsilon
              const EPS = 0.01 * GEOM_SCALE;
              if (bx < -EPS || by < -EPS || bx + bw > scaledSheet.width + EPS || by + bh > scaledSheet.height + EPS) {
                  return false;
              }
      
              for (const placed of placedParts) {
                  if (placed === part) continue;
                  const pb = placed.getBounds();
                  if (bx > pb.x + pb.width || bx + bw < pb.x ||
                      by > pb.y + pb.height || by + bh < pb.y) {
                      continue;
                  }
                  if (placed.lcolor === "#00ff00") {
                      if (GeometryUtil.polyOutside(part, placed)) {
                          return false;
                      }
                      continue;
                  }
                  if (part.polygonsIntersect(placed, true)) {
                      return false;
                  }
              }
              return true;
          }
      }

              for (let i = 1; i < len; i++) {
                  const point = path0[i];
                  x = point.x;
                  y = point.y;
      
                  if (x < minX) minX = x;
                  else if (x > maxX) maxX = x;
      
                  if (y < minY) minY = y;
                  else if (y > maxY) maxY = y;

  function cmdClone() {
    if (xfBlock()) return;
    const supported = new Set(['line', 'arc', 'circle', 'spline', 'text', 'art']);
    // resolved through the same cascade the export paths use: a marquee selects
    // points, and the entities those points fully cover are what it means
    const picked = selectedEntitiesForExport().filter(e => supported.has(e.type));
    if (!picked.length) {
      toast('Select the shapes to clone');
      return;
    }
    // Drop only the guide lines a framed object OWNS (group/array/text frames) —
    // cloning those would duplicate construction geometry nobody asked for. A
    // green line the user drew themselves is real geometry and must be cloneable,
    // which is why the colour alone cannot decide this (see ownedGuideIds).
    const guides = ownedGuideIds();
    const masters = picked.filter(e => !guides.has(+e.id)).map(e => +e.id);
    if (!masters.length) {
      toast('Select the shapes to clone, not the owned guide lines');
      return;
    }
    // Every Clone makes its OWN entity. Pooling the copies of one master into a
    // single array meant they selected, moved and transformed as one lump — the
    // opposite of "place three copies and arrange each one".
    // The new instance lands one bounding-box to the right of the master, which
    // is the placement a copy usually wants and is trivially editable after.
    const b = selectionBounds();
    const gap = 10;
    const shift = b ? (b.maxX - b.minX) + gap : 50;
    const mat = [1, 0, 0, 1, shift, 0];
    // remember the master anchor at THIS moment: the offset the master gains
    // later is cancelled at render time, so the copy stays put when the master
    // is moved (see cloneInstanceOffsets).
    const anchorObj = {
      m: mat
    };
    const anc = (() => {
      for (const id of masters) {
        const m = state.entities[id];
        if (!m) continue;
        const ids = entityPointIds(m);
        if (!ids.length) continue;
        const p = P(ids[0]);
        if (p) return [p.x, p.y];
      }
      return null;
    })();
    if (anc) anchorObj.a = anc;

    pushHistory();
    const id = newId();
    state.entities[id] = {
      id, type: 'array', kind: 'clone',
      params: {}, color: colorOf(picked[0]), layer: ui.activeLayer,
      masters, instances: [anchorObj]
    };
    delete state.entities[id].shapes;
    ui.selection = [{ kind: 'entity', id }];
    invalidateLoops();
    commit();
    toast('Cloned — edit the master to reshape it, R to place it');
  }

  function arrayInstanceOffsets(e) {
    const out = [];
    if (e.kind === 'clone') return cloneInstanceOffsets(e);
    const p = e.params || {};
    if (e.kind === 'guide') {
      const n = Math.max(1, Math.floor(+p.count || 1));
      const guideE = e.guideId != null ? state.entities[e.guideId] : null;
      if (!guideE || n < 2) return out;
      // flatten the guide entity to a polyline path
      const polys = entityWorldPolylines(guideE);
      if (!polys.length || !polys[0].pts || polys[0].pts.length < 2) return out;
      const path = polys[0].pts;
      // compute cumulative arc-length for even distribution
      const lens = [0];
      for (let i = 1; i < path.length; i++) {
        lens.push(lens[i - 1] + Math.hypot(path[i].x - path[i - 1].x, path[i].y - path[i - 1].y));
      }
      const total = lens[lens.length - 1];
      if (total < 1e-9) return out;
      // interpolate along path by arc-length parameter
      const at = (t) => {
        const target = t * total;
        let i = 1;
        while (i < lens.length - 1 && lens[i] < target) i++;
        const seg = lens[i] - lens[i - 1];
        const f = seg > 1e-9 ? (target - lens[i - 1]) / seg : 0;
        const a = path[i - 1], b = path[i];
        return { x: a.x + (b.x - a.x) * f, y: a.y + (b.y - a.y) * f, seg: i - 1, f };
      };
      const master0 = at(0);
      const rotate = !!p.rotate;
      for (let k = 1; k < n; k++) {
        const t = k / (n - 1);
        const pt = at(t);

          // rotation centre: where the clone lands on the guide
          o.cx = pt.x;
          o.cy = pt.y;
        }
        out.push(o);

> _Reasoning_
> Important: MiniSketch has a "clone" feature implemented as an `array` entity with `kind: 'clone'`, which references masters and stores instance offsets. The user says "memanfaatkan fitur clone dari minisketch" — meaning use the clone mechanism to produce the nested copies (masters stay where green sheet is, instances placed at nested positions). That's a key design decision: nesting output should create ONE clone array entity per... hmm. Actually clone entity supports `masters` (multiple ids) and `instances` (each an offset matrix applied to all masters). So a nesting result = one clone array entity with all selected loop entities as masters and one instance per nested placement. But each placement has different rotation, and clone offsets only support dx,dy,ang,cx,cy? Let me check cloneInstanceOffsets to see supported transform fields.

> Also, the selected objects may include arcs/splines with constraints; clones are render-time copies of masters (not separate entities), which is ideal for nesting output (non-destructive) but maybe not ideal for "place output in worksheet". Hmm, but the user explicitly wants "memanfaatkan fitur clone" so nested parts are clones of the selected loops. However, clones copy the master shape as-is; the nesting needs compound loops (outer + holes). A clone array with multiple masters as one rigid group would move all masters together — not what nesting needs (each part placed independently with own rotation). So we need one clone entity per part? That means one clone array per master with one instance. Let's read cloneInstanceOffsets and how clone entities render/hit-test, and whether instances support rotation.

        function nestPlaceAt(ir, pt) {

          svgImportInsert(ir, { center: pt });
